name: Stormchaser's Talent
assumptions: The base ability (from root nodes B/C→D) is printed with no "Level 1 —" header, matching how the leveling structure implies only levels 2 and 3 carry an explicit cost header (E and I each carry a cond:class_level=N + cost: flag; the base level does not).

Node F's trigger-type: "classlevelgained" was worded as "Whenever you level up this Class" — the node names the event type but not its literal printed phrasing; this is the standard phrasing for that trigger concept.

Nodes J and K (two separate spellcast trigger nodes, for instant and sorcery respectively) were merged into one printed ability, "Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell, create a 1/1 blue and red Otter creature token," since both converge on the identical continuation (L) and produce no distinguishable effect from each other. Note the schema explicitly treats a shared downstream node as a "real fact, not a bug to resolve into one path," so this merge is a templating judgment call, not something the graph itself dictates — unlike G/H, which are covered by an actual combine: "any" group and so are unambiguously one flexible action ("instant or sorcery card").
couldNotDerive: Supertype and rarity — withheld/not present in the registries or nodes, left blank rather than guessed.
notes:
Real card confirmed via forge-model/data/stormchaser-s-talent.txt: Stormchaser's Talent, {U} Enchantment — Class. Oracle: "When Stormchaser's Talent enters, create a 1/1 blue and red Otter creature token with prowess. {3}{U}: Level 2 -- When this Class becomes level 2, return target instant or sorcery card from your graveyard to your hand. {5}{U}: Level 3 -- Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell, create a 1/1 blue and red Otter creature token with prowess." Mana cost, type line, both level-up costs (E: cost:{3}{U} cond:class_level=2; I: cost:{5}{U} cond:class_level=3), the ETB token creation, the level-3 cast-trigger token creation, and the level-2 graveyard-return chapter all reconstructed correctly, with meaning matching in every case despite minor phrasing differences ("Level 2 -- {3}{U}" vs "{3}{U}: Level 2"; "Whenever you level up this Class" vs "When this Class becomes level 2" -- both name the same classlevelgained/ClassLevelGained event).

Translator fix confirmed working: this packet's nodes G (gy->hand, thing:instant, flags:target) and H (gy->hand, thing:sorcery, flags:target) are now joined under flow.steps.F = [{combine:"any", of:[G,H]}], where attempts 1-2 apparently exposed them as two independent sibling steps. The examiner correctly read the combine:"any" group as one disjunctive target ("return target instant or sorcery card from your graveyard to your hand"), an exact semantic match to the real ValidTgts$ Instant.YouCtrl,Sorcery.YouCtrl on a single ChangeZone effect. No residual sign of the old two-independent-steps misreading (e.g. no "return target instant card... and return target sorcery card..." double-effect artifact). This closes out the decomposition gap that motivated the first two attempts.

One open issue remains, and it is the deliberately deferred one called out in the task brief rather than a new finding: the otter-1 token registry entry (labels: creature/token/blue/red, stats 1/1, subtype Otter) carries no field for token-printed keyword abilities, so both token-creation abilities in the reconstruction read "1/1 blue and red Otter creature token" with no "with prowess" clause, while the real card's token has prowess in both places it's created. This is a registry/schema gap (no place to hang a keyword-ability tag on a `labels` token template), not an agent misinterpretation or a fresh decomposition gap in this card's own edges -- the agent had no way to derive prowess from what it was given, and correctly omitted rather than invented it. Per the task instructions this is expected and does not count against an otherwise-correct reconstruction; verdict is "issues-open" solely to record this known, still-outstanding registry limitation for tracking, not because anything about the card's edges or flow needs further translator work.
